solutionReview.headline: One doubling every {{d}} hours means the exponent is $\frac{t}{{{d}}}$: $P(t)={{A}}(2)^{t/{{d}}}$.
reasoning: The population starts at {{A}} and is multiplied by 2 once every {{d}} hours, so after $t$ hours it has doubled $\frac{t}{{{d}}}$ times.
Check: at $t={{d}}$ the exponent is $\frac{{{d}}}{{{d}}}=1$, and the population is ${{A}}\cdot 2={{A2}}$, double the start.
solutionReview.commonError: Multiplying the exponent by {{d}} instead of dividing, or adding a fixed amount each hour: doubling multiplies.

solutionReview.headline: Growing by {{p}}% multiplies by $\frac{{{factor}}}{100}$ each year.
reasoning: Increasing by {{p}}% keeps the whole value and adds {{p}}%: $100\%+{{p}}\%={{factor}}\%$, so each year the value is multiplied by $\frac{{{factor}}}{100}$.
Starting at {{A}} dollars: $V(t)={{A}}\left(\dfrac{{{factor}}}{100}\right)^t$.
